candidates.name: ScraperHub/agoda-property-listing-scraper

candidates.why_useful: Could be a one-command pull for Agoda listing counts/prices in APAC markets as a competitor-supply proxy (gap #9), if run against a public source and consistent with ToS.

candidates.name: factden/agoda-hotel-reviews-scraper

candidates.why_useful: Review volume/velocity by traveler type and stay date on Agoda could proxy APAC travel demand seasonality, complementary to the Booking.com review datasets already held.

candidates.name: bondvit/agoda-scraper-examples
candidates.what_it_holds: Runnable Python & JS examples calling the Agoda Hotel Scraper on Apify; example output snippets only, no bulk data.

candidates.name: everythingscraper/trip-hotel-scraper

candidates.why_useful: Trip.com/Ctrip is the dominant APAC OTA; a working price/availability puller could be adapted for a point-in-time APAC hotel-rate panel not otherwise available (gaps #2, #9).

candidates.name: factden/ctrip-trip-reviews-scraper

candidates.why_useful: Could support a review-based 'stays index' analogue for Chinese/APAC outbound travel, similar to the team's existing Inside Airbnb reviews-index method (gap #9).

candidates.name: factden/qunar-hotel-reviews-scraper

candidates.why_useful: Qunar is a large Chinese domestic-travel OTA; reviews could proxy domestic China lodging demand, an otherwise dark region for the team (gap #9, #7).

candidates.name: factden/makemytrip-scraper

candidates.why_useful: India is a fast-growing APAC short-term-lodging market with no coverage in the team's current holdings; hotel sub-ratings and review velocity could proxy Indian travel demand.

candidates.name: 2892480843/CityPulse
candidates.what_it_holds: AI agent for predicting emerging/trending destination cities for Qunar (Ctrip-owned Chinese OTA) with a scoring/backtest architecture. Data files (city_score_snapshot.csv, daily_signal_sample.csv, signals_demo_panel.csv: 13 cities x 45 days x 9 indicators = 5,031 rows, feature_dictionary.csv, reference_sources.csv) are explicitly labeled SYNTHETIC/demo, not real Qunar order data. MIT license, 32 commits.
candidates.why_useful: The METHOD (a documented multi-signal, time-cutoff-validated nowcasting architecture for city-level Chinese travel demand) could be a template even though the data itself is fake; not a data source.

candidates.name: chuqinyao/citypulse-ai-qunar-2026
candidates.what_it_holds: Competition entry (2026) using time-series signals to forecast trending Qunar destinations; data is explicitly is_synthetic=true, 12 cities x 180 days = 2,160 rows, no real Qunar order data. MIT license, 7 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat as CityPulse above — a nowcasting-method reference only, not usable as a data source; documents rolling 7/14/28-day feature construction that could inspire a MIDAS-style APAC demand nowcast (gap #17).

notes: This scout's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) session-wide before any query of mine ran, and gh search was disallowed for this modality per instructions, so all four Google-style WebSearch queries failed immediately. DuckDuckGo HTML fetches hit a CAPTCHA wall; Bing fetches returned irrelevant/generic results (looked like cached/mismatched pages, possibly geo/bot-filtered). I fell back entirely to WebFetch on github.com/topics/<tag> pages (these worked reliably) and direct repo URLs; github.com/search?q=... consistently 429'd with Retry-After 3600, so I could not run true keyword searches across all of GitHub — only topic-tag browsing, which undercounts repos that didn't self-tag. Xiaozhu, Tujia, Meituan, MakeMyTrip, and OYO all show essentially no public GitHub datasets with real, non-synthetic transaction data — they exist mostly as scraper/clone/tooling repos, consistent with these platforms being harder to reach from outside China or India. The two 'CityPulse' Qunar repos looked promising (built specifically to forecast Chinese destination-city travel demand) but both explicitly self-disclose 100%-synthetic data, so they are method references only, not data. If another scout has `gh` access or a working WebSearch budget, re-run 'site:github.com agoda|ctrip|tujia|meituan|makemytrip|oyo|traveloka dataset' directly — I could not complete this most basic query type this run. Also worth a Kaggle/Zenodo-specific scout pass (not attempted here) for 'MakeMyTrip', 'OYO Rooms', and 'Ctrip' since Kaggle notebooks/datasets often link back to GitHub companion repos I could not discover via topic-browsing alone.
